toc.title: The vocabulary of AI, from AI to deep learning, inference and data
Fit, bias, LLMs, agents and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; ML: machine learning; LLM: large language model

  • Define the basic terms: AI, ML, deep learning, neural network, model, algorithm, training and inference
  • Name the fields of AI: computer vision, natural language processing (NLP) and speech recognition
  • Tell the types of inference, the types of data and the types of learning apart
  • Explain bias, fairness and fit
  • Separate LLMs, generative AI and agentic AI from the rest

2The vocabulary of AI, from AI to deep learning, inference and data

Running case

Cedar and Salt Hears the Buzzwords

  • At Cedar and Salt, leaders keep saying AI, ML, GenAI and agents as if they were one thing
  • The product team wants a shared vocabulary before it picks any tool
  • First question: what is each term, and how do they relate?
  • Your job: give the team clear definitions and a way to tell them apart

How AI, ML and Deep Learning Fit Together

  • Artificial intelligence (AI): technology that lets machines do human-like problem-solving tasks
  • Machine learning (ML): a branch of AI that learns from data instead of following explicit instructions
  • Deep learning: ML that uses neural networks with many layers
  • Generative AI (GenAI): an advanced form of deep learning that creates new content
  • Not all AI is ML: AI is the umbrella term

Exam tip

Nesting from outside in: AI, then ML, then deep learning, then generative AI.

Machine Learning, Models and Algorithms

  • ML analyzes data without explicit instructions: it learns patterns from examples
  • An algorithm is the method that learns from the data
  • A model is the result: the learned patterns, stored in its parameters
  • Training is the learning step; the model is then tested on data it has not seen
  • A trained model takes new input and gives an output, such as a prediction
Exam tip

The algorithm is the recipe; the model is what the recipe produces after training.

Neural Networks and Deep Learning

  • A neural network is inspired by the human brain: many connected artificial neurons
  • It has an input layer, one or more hidden layers and an output layer
  • Deep learning uses networks with many layers
  • It can process unstructured data, such as images, speech and text, without manual feature extraction
  • It needs a lot of data and computing power
Exam tip

"Deep" in deep learning means many layers.

The Fields of AI: Vision, Language and Speech

Field What it does Example at Cedar and Salt
Computer vision Extracts information from images and video Spotting a damaged room in a photo
Natural language processing (NLP) Interprets and understands human language in text Finding the sentiment of a review
Speech recognition Turns spoken words into text and finds meaning Transcribing a customer call
  • Machine translation, named-entity recognition and sentiment analysis are NLP tasks
  • Recommendation systems, fraud detection and forecasting are other common AI uses
Exam tip

Pictures: computer vision. Written language: NLP. Spoken words to text: speech recognition.

Training and Inference

  • Training: the model learns from data; it takes time and compute
  • Inference: the trained model is used on new input to give a prediction or an answer
  • Training happens before use; inference happens every time the model is used
  • Most of the ongoing cost of a live application is inference

Exam tip

Training builds the model; inference uses it.

Types of Inference [Verify live]

Type How it works Fits when
Real-time An always-on endpoint answers each request quickly Interactive, low-latency needs
Serverless No infrastructure to manage; scales with traffic Idle periods between bursts; cold starts are acceptable
Asynchronous Requests are queued and processed later Large payloads (up to 1 GB) and long processing (up to 1 hour)
Batch A job runs the model over a whole dataset No persistent endpoint is needed
  • As of 5 November 2026: the limits shown are from the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation
Exam tip

Instant answers: real-time. Whole dataset, no endpoint: batch. Large or slow requests: asynchronous.

Types of Data

Kind of data Meaning Example
Labeled Each example has the right answer attached Reviews tagged positive or negative
Unlabeled Examples without answers Raw reviews with no tags
Structured / tabular Rows and columns with a fixed layout A bookings table
Time-series Values recorded over time Daily bookings per month
Unstructured No fixed layout: text, images, audio, video Photos and call recordings
Exam tip

Labeled data has answers; structured data has a fixed layout. They are different questions.

Types of Learning

Learning type Learns from Goal
Supervised Labeled data Predict a known kind of answer: a category or a number
Unsupervised Unlabeled data Find patterns or groups by itself
Reinforcement Rewards for its actions Learn the best sequence of steps toward a goal
  • Semi-supervised learning mixes a little labeled data with a lot of unlabeled data Beyond the guide
  • Supervised: classification and regression. Unsupervised: clustering. Reinforcement: reward and goal
Exam tip

Labels given: supervised. No labels: unsupervised. Reward signal: reinforcement.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's First Vocabulary

Cedar and Salt needs to It is
Read a guest review and find the sentiment NLP
Spot a damaged room in a photo Computer vision
Transcribe a recorded call Speech recognition
Score tonight's bookings with no endpoint running Batch inference
Group guests into segments with no labels Unsupervised learning
Predict cancellations from past labeled bookings Supervised learning
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Fit, bias, LLMs, agents and practice

Fit: Underfitting, Overfitting and a Good Fit

  • Underfitting: the model is too simple; it does poorly on training data and new data; high bias
  • Good fit: it captures the main pattern and works on new data too
  • Overfitting: it memorizes the training data and fails on new data; high variance
  • Fix underfitting with a more capable model or better features; fix overfitting with more data or a simpler model

Exam tip

Great on training data but poor on new data: overfitting.

Bias and Fairness

  • Bias in AI is a systematic error that favors or harms some outcomes or groups
  • It often comes from unrepresentative data or from choices in the model
  • Fairness means the system treats different groups equitably
  • Biased data can make biased predictions, even when the model is accurate overall
  • Bias and fairness are covered in depth in Module 11
Exam tip

Biased data in, biased predictions out.

Large Language Models and Generative AI

  • Generative AI creates new content: text, images, audio, video and code
  • A foundation model (FM) is trained on broad, unlabeled data and handles many tasks
  • A large language model (LLM) is a very large deep learning model pre-trained on huge amounts of text
  • Most LLMs use the transformer design and have billions of parameters
  • An LLM predicts the next token, which lets it write, summarize, translate and answer questions
Exam tip

Every LLM is a foundation model for language, and a foundation model is a form of generative AI.

Agentic AI

  • Agentic AI is an autonomous AI system that acts independently to reach pre-set goals
  • It is goal-driven: it plans steps, uses tools and adapts as new information arrives
  • It keeps memory so that long tasks stay consistent
  • Ordinary software follows fixed rules; an assistant that only answers a prompt is not yet agentic
  • Modules 4 and 7 cover how agents are built
Exam tip

Autonomy, goals, tools and memory are the signs of agentic AI.

Telling Them Apart

Term In one line Key word
AI Machines doing human-like problem solving Umbrella
ML AI that learns from data Patterns
Deep learning ML with many-layer neural networks Layers
Generative AI Deep learning that creates content New content
Agentic AI AI that acts toward goals with tools Autonomy
Exam tip

Pick the key word in the question: umbrella, patterns, layers, new content or autonomy.

What the Exam Asks: Core Concepts

  • Which term: AI, ML, deep learning, GenAI or agentic AI, from a short description
  • Which field: computer vision, NLP or speech recognition
  • Which inference: real-time, serverless, asynchronous or batch
  • Which data: labeled or unlabeled, structured or unstructured, time-series
  • Which learning: supervised, unsupervised or reinforcement
  • Which problem: underfitting, overfitting or bias
Exam tip

Name the situation first, then the term.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which statement correctly describes how AI, machine learning and deep learning relate?

  • AMachine learning is a branch of AI, and deep learning is machine learning with many-layer neural networks
  • BDeep learning is the umbrella term, and AI is one narrow technique used inside machine learning models
  • CAI and machine learning are two names for exactly the same field, and neither includes deep learning
  • DDeep learning is a separate field of AI that never uses neural networks of any kind in its models
Show the answer

Answer: A. AI is the umbrella, machine learning is a branch of it that learns from data, and deep learning is machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers. The other options reverse or confuse the relationship.

S2Cedar and Salt wants to score last month's bookings for cancellation risk in one overnight job, and it does not want an endpoint left running. Which type of inference fits best?

  • AReal-time inference, with an always-on endpoint
  • BBatch inference, which runs the model over a whole dataset
  • CServerless inference, which scales with request traffic
  • DAsynchronous inference, which queues individual large requests
Show the answer

Answer: B. Batch inference runs a model over a complete dataset without a persistent endpoint. Real-time and serverless serve individual requests as they arrive, and asynchronous inference queues large or slow individual requests.

S3Which TWO of these are examples of unstructured data? (Select TWO.)

  • APhotos of hotel rooms
  • BA table of bookings with fixed columns
  • CRecordings of customer calls
  • DA spreadsheet of daily totals
  • EA list of prices in a database table
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Images and audio have no fixed row-and-column layout, so they are unstructured. Tables, spreadsheets and database rows are structured or tabular data.

S4A model scores very well on its training data but poorly on new bookings. What is the most likely problem?

  • AUnderfitting, with high bias
  • BToo little compute for inference
  • CToo many labeled examples in the data
  • DOverfitting, with high variance
Show the answer

Answer: D. A model that memorizes its training data but fails on new data is overfitting, which shows as high variance. Underfitting would do poorly on both the training data and new data.

S5Cedar and Salt builds an assistant that sets its own steps toward a booking goal, uses tools such as search and payment, and remembers the traveler's earlier choices. Which term describes it best?

  • AAgentic AI
  • BComputer vision
  • CUnsupervised learning
  • DBatch inference
Show the answer

Answer: A. Autonomy, goals, tool use and memory are the signs of agentic AI. Computer vision works on images, unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data, and batch inference runs a model over a dataset.

S6The team groups guests into segments by behavior, and none of the guests has a label. Which type of learning is this?

  • ASupervised learning
  • BReinforcement learning
  • CUnsupervised learning
  • DTransfer inference
Show the answer

Answer: C. Finding groups in data without labels is unsupervised learning, usually clustering. Supervised learning needs labeled examples, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards for actions.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Nesting AI, ML, deep learning, generative AI; agentic AI acts toward goals
Model an algorithm trained on data produces a model; training builds it, inference uses it
Inference real-time, serverless, asynchronous and batch
Data and learning labeled or not, structured or not; supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement
Fit underfitting is high bias; overfitting is high variance
LLMs huge deep learning models trained on text, predicting the next token
